name: Rhythm in Residence

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 9 / title.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 9 / page.

recognitionRules: Use a percussion-inspired cover with clear reading fields over the artwork.
Pair Georgia statements with Arial practical detail.
Use the deep plum cover with cream type, pink rhythm accents and the source swirling percussion artwork; lighter reading areas retain plum ink.
Show an eight-count practice sequence with taps and rests equally legible.

principles: Use short action sentences; follow an invitation with a concrete material, choice or check.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Eight counts. A place for sound, and a place for silence.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid promises that every participant will master the skill.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Try one version, then compare it with the criterion.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use RHYTHM IN RESIDENCE in Georgia beside eight small marks with one deliberate rest. Keep the rhythm schematic and text-labeled in teaching materials.
invariants: Use a percussion-inspired cover with clear reading fields over the artwork.
Pair Georgia statements with Arial practical detail.
Use the deep plum cover with cream type, pink rhythm accents and the source swirling percussion artwork; lighter reading areas retain plum ink.
adaptations: A programme can use the full rhythmic line; small labels use only the name.
Practice sheets prioritize counting over cover artwork.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
